statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Portal de Servicios en Línea (Trámite de Reserva de Nombre de Sociedad Anónima)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official legal language of the registry; a proposed name may be in Spanish or any Latin-script language provided it is transliterated into Roman characters; the name shall not be misleading as to the corporate objects, nationality, or regulated nature of the business; all applicable corporate forms of the Sociedad Anónima shall use the closing expression 'S.A.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five business days of the adverse name resolution, the applicant or its resident agent may file a written reconsideration request with the Registro Público de Panamá - Registro de Nombres, attaching the previous decision, the proposed alternative trademark search report, and any notarial consent or trademark coexistence letter from the owner of a conflicting registered name. If the reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal may be filed before the Superior Tribunal de Cuentas or the competent administrative litigation chamber of the Circuit Court of Panama within ten business days, and, if required, a judicial action may be pursued before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a non-regulated proprietary trader and wholesale distribution entity, subject to the mandatory appointment of a licensed Panamanian resident agent with a physical address in Panama; the resident agent's physical office serves as the official registered office and service-of-process address, while a virtual office or business mailbox may be used for administrative and commercial correspondence; no virtual office can replace the registered agent or the registered office address recorded with the Registro Público.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate: for a low-risk cross-border matcha powder trading company utilizing Swift_TT and Wire_Transfer payment rails, the quantified annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Registro Público, DGI, or UAF is approximately 5-8%, with the likelihood increasing if UBO declarations are inconsistent, local substance indicators are disproportionate to revenue, or unusual transaction patterns appear in banking records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Corporation Law for Sociedades Anónimas), as amended, Articles 1 through 66; supplementary rules of the Registro Público de Panamá and the Código Fiscal where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Registro de Personas Jurídicas
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Articles of Incorporation / Pacto Social) executed before a Panamanian Notary and inscribed in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or bank deposit requirement. Standard capital structure is an authorized capital of USD 10,000 divided into 10,000 ordinary shares of USD 1.00 par value; subscribed capital may be credited as fully paid by members without physical contribution evidence. The Public Registry inscription tariff is calculated on the declared authorized capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors approves the issuance and subscription of ten thousand (10,000) ordinary shares with a par value of US$1.00 each, in favor of the founding subscribers, credited as fully paid and non-assessable. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is established at [Registered Office Address, Panama City, Republic of Panama]; and [Resident Agent] S.A. is appointed as the Corporation's resident agent. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed as President, [Name] as Treasurer, and [Name] as Secretary, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the President, Secretary, and resident agent, jointly and severally, are authorized to execute the Articles of Incorporation, pay applicable registry fees, and complete all legal filings necessary to duly incorporate the Corporation and register it with the appropriate authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Ventanilla de Personas Jurídicas (online and in-person)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a formal name search request for the proposed Sociedad Anónima denomination to verify that no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered. The Registry issues a Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre, which must be presented with the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Name search application form
Passport or national ID copy of the applicant/promoter
Power of attorney if submitted through a legal representative or law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, promptly submit a new name search with alternative names; no formal appeal is required, refiling is immediate and the clearance certificate is reissued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Escritura Pública de Constitución Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública, Panama City (authorized notarial protocol)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social) including the corporate name, main purpose (cross-border distribution of organic matcha powder and food products), authorized capital, term, and governance structure. Incorporators and the appointed resident agent execute the deed before a Panamanian notary; the notary retains the original in the protocol and issues certified copies for registration.
required_dossiers: Name clearance certificate from the Public Registry
Draft Articles of Incorporation with corporate purpose per ISIC 4631
Passport or ID copies of incorporators and initial subscribers
Written acceptance of the resident agent appointment
Corporate capital and share allocation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Minor drafting errors are cured by an aclaración deed executed before the same notary; material amendments require a new notarial instrument filed prior to inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Corporation in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Registro de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first certified copy of the Escritura Pública together with the tariff payment form to the Public Registry. The Registry examines the deed for legal compliance, assigns a Ficha (corporate file) and an inscription number, and records the legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima.
required_dossiers: First certified copy (primera copia) of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Completed tariff declaration form for inscription rights
Payment receipt of the registry inscription fee
Certified copy of the name clearance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrador issues a nota de objeción or defecto, file a written response addressing each objection; if a substantive defect is found, correct the deed by a notarial amendment and resubmit the instrument within the statutory term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Identification (RUC/NIT) Registration with the Dirección General de Ingresos
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – RUC Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Public Registry inscription number is assigned, register the S.A. with the DGI to obtain the RUC/NIT corporate tax identification number. File the tax registration form, provide the legal representative's identification, and designate the tax domicile for territorial tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Escritura Pública and Ficha
RUC registration application form
Passport or ID of the legal representative
Proof of appointment of the legal representative or power of attorney
Registered office address verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries or rejects the application for missing or inconsistent data, submit the omitted corporate documents through the DGI ventanilla or online portal; administrative corrections follow the Código Fiscal remedial procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Post-Formation Corporate Governance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá, Alcaldía – Ventanilla de Aviso de Operación; Secretariat of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal Aviso de Operación (business operation notice) for the commercial activity of wholesale distribution of food products. Concurrently, maintain the corporate minute book, share register, and statutory records at the registered office, and ensure the resident agent keeps the official copy of the corporate register.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate issued by DGI
Copy of inscribed Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of the registered office address
Identity document of the legal representative
Description of commercial premises for municipal inspection, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality objects to the Aviso de Operación, correct the declared commercial activity code and resubmit; municipal decisions are appealable before the Mayor or the local Administrative Tribunal in accordance with municipal tax law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección de Fiscalización de Comercios; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección de Regulación de Alimentos y Bebidas
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial manufacturing license required for wholesale distribution of organic matcha powder; sanitary registration (Registro Sanitario de Alimentos) and commercial import/export registration under MICI procedures apply to the physical movement of food commodities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category I – no significant environmental impact). Pure trading and warehousing activity without manufacturing, processing, or effluent generation does not trigger a full or partial EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply. If a temperature-controlled warehouse is operated, food-grade storage must comply with MINSA sanitary storage regulations; solid waste from spoiled or expired matcha powder must be disposed of through municipal licensed waste channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for any occupied premises; structural load adequacy verification for warehouse racking; and occupational health clearance from Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) for administrative and warehouse personnel, including basic safety training documentation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa) and Sistema de Gestión de Ingresos.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Any Panamanian Sociedad Anónima, including 100% foreign-owned entities, must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) before commencing commercial operations. Procedure: (1) register the S.A. with the Registro Público de Panamá and file the municipal Aviso de Operación with the relevant Alcaldía (e.g., Municipio de Panamá); (2) appoint a resident legal representative and declare a fiscal domicile in Panama through a public deed or private document; (3) submit to the DGI the public incorporation deed, legalization of foreign shareholder/director documents, passport copies, and proof of fiscal address; (4) a domestic bank account and minimum capital deposit are recommended for the corporate record (no legal minimum capital exists); (5) the DGI issues the RUC certificate, which simultaneously enrolls the entity for income tax (ISR), ITBMS, and withholding obligations. Processing time: approximately 5–10 business days. Foreign-source-only trading entities may register as 'exportador' or remain passive RUC holders where no local taxable activity occurs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope — the Panamanian S.A. is a taxable entity under the classical system; Panamanian ISR (Impuesto sobre la Renta) applies only to Panama-source income. Foreign-source income (procurement and resale of matcha powder entirely outside Panama, with title, risk, and payment located abroad) is exempt from ISR and dividends paid from such income are not subject to Panamanian withholding. Exception: under Law 22 of 2010, the entity loses territoriality and becomes taxable on worldwide income if 50% or more of its shares are owned by Panamanian residents or 50% or more of its gross income derives from transactions with Panamanian residents. No pass-through default exists; the optional transparency regime may apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not employ U.S.-style check-the-box classification; the following statutory elections are available: (a) Optional Fiscal Transparency Election (Ley 22 de 2010, Art. 4) — an entity deriving 80%+ foreign-source income may elect transparent treatment, attributing income to shareholders and enabling foreign tax credit preservation; (b) SEM / Multinational Headquarters Regime (Ley 41 de 2007) — for regional headquarters providing services to related parties, granting 0% tax on qualifying services; (c) Zona Libre de Colón operator license — goods physically entering the free zone benefit from a separate territorial exemption regime; (d) Panama-Pacifico and Ciudad del Saber special tax incentive elections; (e) Small Taxpayer Fixed-Fee Scheme (Ley 42 de 2014) for annual turnover at or below USD 36,000.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's Value-Added Tax type levy on transfers of movable goods and services, Law 6 of 2005 as amended by Law 8 of 2010 and Código Fiscal Arts. 1850–1912).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis registration threshold — every person engaged in taxable transfers of goods or services in Panamanian territory must register for ITBMS prior to commencement. Small taxpayers with annual gross sales up to USD 36,000 (approx.) may elect the fixed monthly quota regime of Law 42 of 2014. An offshore matcha trading vehicle whose goods never enter Panamanian customs territory is not engaged in taxable local transfers and is not required to collect ITBMS, although RUC enrolment remains advisable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing via the SFEP (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá). All ITBMS-registered taxpayers must issue standardized XML e-invoices authenticated by the taxpayer's digital signature (Firma Electrónica), transmit invoices to the DGI platform in real time (or same-day batch transmission) through Sede Electrónica or certified billing software, obtain a computerized DGI acknowledgment (Acuse de Recibo), and print a QR code with authenticity verification. Pre-printed prefixed paper invoices are restricted to small taxpayers using simplified tiquete machines or the fixed-quota regime. Export invoices must be flagged 'Exportación' at 0% ITBMS and reference the supporting customs document.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are subject to ITBMS at 0%. For the Matcha Powder Distribution model, three factual patterns support zero-rating: (a) direct physical export from Panama — requires valid DEX customs exit and transport documents; (b) transit through Zona Libre de Colón — requires ZLC entry/exit documentation evidencing that goods were not sold for domestic consumption; (c) pure offshore drop-shipment (goods shipped from origin country directly to the non-resident buyer, never entering Panama) — supported by placement of contract, risk and title outside Panama, foreign-source payment, and absence of any local taxable event; this pattern simultaneously safeguards territorial ISR treatment. The zero-rated invoice and ITBMS credit refunds are available for related local logistics, warehousing, and professional costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX — Declaración de Exportación) generated by SIA/despacho aduanero
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (including through B/L for offshore transshipment)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 credit advice from the non-resident buyer
Commercial invoice and packing list stating INCOTERMS and foreign destination
Certificate of Origin and phytosanitary/ceremonial-grade certification of matcha from the exporting origin country
Copy of the procurement contract proving title transfer outside Panama
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama is fully dollarized with no exchange controls and no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure reflects standard documentary-export banking and DGI audit expectation for settlement of foreign receivables. Penalties for abusive export zero-rating or sham foreign-sourcing structures: DGI may retroactively claw back zero-rated/refunded ITBMS with monthly surcharges (1.5% per month on the unpaid tax) and compensatory interest; fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the suppressed tax under Código Fiscal Art. 751 and Law 6 of 2005; criminal tax fraud referral with imprisonment of 2 to 5 years (Código Fiscal Arts. 762–767); and retroactive requalification of foreign-source income as Panama-source under Law 22 of 2010 with assessment up to the 4-year statute of limitations (extended to 6 years where no return was filed). Export refund claims are subject to 100% documentary verification by the DGI before payment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no issuing central bank. Banking, AML/CFT, and prudential supervision is exercised exclusively by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Decree-Law 2 of 2008 and Law 23 of 2015. Banco Nacional de Panamá acts exclusively as fiscal agent of the State and manager of public funds, without monetary authority powers. Domestic currency issuance is limited to Balboa-denominated coins (PAB, minted by the U.S. Mint), while the U.S. dollar (USD) circulates as full legal tender under the country's de jure policy of dollarization adopted via the Currency Law of 1904.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama maintains full, unconditional dollarization with no exchange-control regime. The U.S. dollar serves as circulating medium, unit of account, and legal tender in unlimited amounts; the Balboa is a subsidiary denomination at a fixed 1:1 parity. Panama is an IMF Article VIII member and imposes no restrictions on current international transactions, no capital-account controls, no central-bank currency permits, and no investment or profit-repatriation authorization. Dividends, branch remittances, and trade proceeds may be freely transferred in USD without approval from the SBP, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), or Panama's Directorate General of Revenue (DGI). The sole practical convertibility or remittance hurdle is the commercial bank's internal AML/KYC clearance under Law 23 of 2015 and the beneficial-ownership transparency requirements of Law 254 of 2021.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no surrender requirement, no compulsory conversion ratio, no domiciliation/repatriation timeline, and no identification requirement for export proceeds. Because USD is legal tender, export receipts of organic matcha powder from Panamanian territory (or, in the case of pass-through trade, non-Panamanian source income of a Panama S.A.) are retained freely in USD. Customs filings through the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) single-window system serve statistical, tariff, and trade-compliance purposes only and do not affect FX convertibility or treasury liquidity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Panama does not maintain a dedicated electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing regime; no entity may passport an offshore EMI license (e.g., UK FCA, EU PSD2 EMI) into Panamanian territory. A Panama S.A. trading matcha may technically open a multi-currency wallet at an unregulated neobank or foreign EMI, but such rails are not compliant primary settlement infrastructure, are frequently rejected by Japanese counterparties and correspondent banks, and generate avoidable AML red flags under Law 23 of 2015. Recommended posture: use a licensed Panamanian bank with full correspondent network for primary settlement; use Fed-wired Treasury-grade fintechs only for information-gathering or disbursement in jurisdictions with local EMI licensing (e.g., UK, Singapore) where the Panama S.A. has established a valid local branch or agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is mandatory in practice. The majority of Tier-1 Panamanian banks (Banco General, Banistmo, Multibank, Global Bank) require at least one natural-person director or the ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person compliance/relationship interview at the Panama City branch. Hybrid onboarding is possible: apostilled corporate documents, notarized board resolutions, and video verification may pre-clear documents, yet the account is typically activated only after physical attendance or a notarized appointment executed at a Panamanian consulate. Fully remote account opening is exceptional and, as of 2024, is effectively unavailable for new non-resident-owned S.A. commercial vehicles; budget for one or two director visits to Panama City to complete onboarding and sign the final mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner opacity: missing declaration of the natural persons controlling the Panama S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified 'Beneficiario Final' filing under Law 254 of 2021 evidenced by Registro Público receipt; corporate stock ledger (Libro de Accionistas); copy of the board resolution appointing the signatories; passport copies of all natural-person shareholders holding greater than 10%; organizational chart showing control chain to natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low capitalization and dormant history: newly acquired shelf S.A. with immediate high-volume matcha trade activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement proving cash contribution; source-of-wealth statement (bank statements, sale of shares, assets); detailed business plan with first-year procurement volume of 2-5 metric tons of matcha and supplier listing; explanation of the S.A.'s inactivity period and the commercial rationale for reactivation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow mismatch: USD inflows from Latin American buyers with supplier settlement to Japan (JPY) and no supporting physical movement through Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supply agreement with the Japanese matcha processor (e.g., Aichi, Kagoshima, Uji cooperative); pro-forma invoice and purchase order; Air Waybill or Bill of Lading evidencing shipment; import/export declarations submitted to the Panamanian ANA or original port authorities; commission or distribution agreement with the off-taker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate FX conversion of USD trade receipts into JPY or rapid layered transfers to third-country accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FX purpose declaration referencing the trade invoice; JPY-denominated accounts payable aging schedule; supplier payment due dates; bank FX deal ticket and internal memo documenting the commercial rationale; sanctions screening report for the Japanese beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border sanctions exposure in distribution chain or presence of PEP-linked intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC, EU, UN, and SBP-maintained sanctions list negative screening of all counterparties; World-Check/TUFF due diligence reports; PEP questionnaire completed by all beneficial owners; contractual Sanctions Compliance and Anti-Bribery representation clause signed by the buyer and supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-identity ambiguity: failure to register the S.A. with the DGI despite operating a commercial treasury in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aviso de Operación (business notice) issued by the DGI; RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) certificate; territoriality analysis showing the matcha procurement is negotiated and executed from Panama as a back-to-back distribution arrangement; if applicable, transfer-pricing documentation for the related-party purchase margin.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders inject USD capital via SWIFT MT103 (or FEDWIRE/CHIPS from U.S. correspondent banks) credited to the Panama S.A.'s operational or escrow USD account at a Panama City bank. The SWIFT field-70 payment reference must state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – SHARE SUBSCRIPTION – ISIC 4631 – COMMERCIAL TRADING'. No SBP, DGI, or foreign-exchange prior approval is required because Panama has no exchange controls; however, the bank will verify sender identity matches the registered shareholder, may provisionally segregate the funds in a capital escrow account until the KYC file is completed, and must record the injection in the corporate share ledger. Commissions and dividends may later be repatriated to shareholders as non-Panamanian-source income subject solely to the territorial tax rules and any applicable dividend-withholding under the Panama Income Tax Code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for trade settlements is outbound SWIFT MT103 in USD from the Panama S.A. bank to the Japanese beneficiary's bank (e.g., MUFG Bank, SMBC, Mizuho), with FX conversion to JPY executed either by the Panamanian bank's international desk or at the receiving correspondent. For large, first-time, or credit-sensitive supplier relationships, utilize an irrevocable, confirmed commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued through the Panama bank's trade desk (with a U.S. or Japanese confirming bank) governed by UCP 600, payable against presentation of commercial invoice, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, weight/packing list, and ocean or air transport documents. Documentary collections (D/P or D/A) are suitable for repeat suppliers. Same-day local liquidity is available through Panama's ACH (Cámara de Compensación) only when the counterparty holds a Panamanian bank account; all cross-border settlement should remain on SWIFT/FEDWIRE rails to preserve evidentiary traceability for the DGI territorial audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/JPY deliverable outright forwards (up to 12-month tenor) executed with the Panamanian bank's international FX desk or a U.S./European correspondent, backed by the underlying matcha import invoice

USD/JPY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Tokyo/WM Reuters fixing, permissible because Panama lacks a domestic interbank FX market and the SBP imposes no restriction on offshore NDF execution
USD/JPY and USD/EUR cross-currency swaps for managing accounts-payable revaluation and refinancing of the working-capital cycle
Vanilla USD/JPY FX options (calls/puts) acquired from a regulated international counterparty to cap procurement cost when the Panama S.A. holds a committed but not yet invoiced supply order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax / Tasa Única Anual — mandatory flat corporate franchise payment for every Sociedad Anónima.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; payment is normally processed through the licensed resident agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on or before 31 March, irrespective of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% surcharge and monthly statutory interest accrue on late payment; after three consecutive unpaid annual periods, the Registro Público may strike the S.A. off the corporate registry and dissolve the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Continuity / Annual Registered Agent Confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá through the resident agent; residency must be continuously maintained under Law 32 of 1927, as amended by Law 5 of 2014.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; agent confirmation is required at each annual franchise payment and whenever the registered office or resident agent changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of the registered agent exposes the company to incapacity, cancellation of good-standing certification, denial of registry filings, and eventual administrative strike-off or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership / Shareholder Register Update Confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent as mandated gatekeeper under Law 23 of 2015, as amended, and Law 5 of 2014; the records are confidential and must be made available to DGI and the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) upon lawful request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed at each corporate anniversary and, in any event, within 30 days after any share transfer or change of ultimate beneficial owner.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may trigger pecuniary fines against the company and its resident agent, suspension of registry filings, and AML/CFT enforcement exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) — required only if the S.A. has Panamanian-source taxable income or is otherwise registered with DGI as an active taxpayer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March following the close of the taxable year for a standard December 31 fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment interest and fines under the Código Fiscal apply; continued non-filing may lead to coercive collection, suspension of the RUC, and denial of tax good-standing certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Panamanian S.A. engaged in matcha-powder distribution must obtain an independent audit and tax opinion (dictamen fiscal) when its Panamanian-source gross annual income exceeds B/.1,000,000 or when its equity/total assets exceed B/.2,000,000. Inactive or purely foreign-trade S.As. below these thresholds are not automatically audited, but DGI, financing parties, or commercial counterparties may nevertheless require reviewed or audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (NIIF); the NIIF para PYMES framework is available to qualifying non-public entities below the DGI audit threshold. Accounting records must be maintained in sufficient detail to allow preparation of financial statements and determination of Panamanian-source taxable income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 23 of 2015 and Law 5 of 2014, the resident agent must obtain and retain an up-to-date beneficial ownership file identifying each natural person who ultimately owns or controls the S.A. Annual written confirmation must be obtained at the corporate anniversary; any share transfer requires the transferor, transferee, and resident agent to formalize the transfer, update the shareholder ledger and the UBO schedule, and issue new share certificates. The register is confidential but must be available to DGI and UAF upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registro de Directores y Funcionarios)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $350–$900 per annum for a Panama licensed resident agent and registered office service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,500–$5,000 per annum for an independent Panamanian CPA audit of a small distribution S.A., excluding DGI tax-opinion preparation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial regime: only Panama-source income taxed; no tax on foreign-source income of the S.A.; 10% surtax on net taxable income exceeding USD 1,500,000 producing marginal effective top rate of 27.5%; Law 52 of 2022 modernization; no general statutory tax holidays for matcha distribution; small taxpayer preferential regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) for gross revenue ≤ USD 200,000 (optional simplified taxation); loss carryforwards 5 years.
